objrepl

Object replication between two nodes from the command line: run a copy, check and compare nodes, take over and rejoin, and a test data generator (DataReel 7.4).

Contents

Usage
Examples

Usage

objrepl primary ROOT --copy HOST[:PORT] --ca CA --cert CERT --key KEY
                [--commits N] [--per N] [--dbs N] [--sleep MS] [--seed N] [--drain] [--no-trim]
                [--drop-linked N] [--unknown-removes N] [--purge] [--defer-target]
objrepl copy ROOT [--listen [ADDR:]PORT|ADDR] --ca CA --cert CERT --key KEY --allow-cn CN
objrepl digest ROOT                every database: ids and content hashes
objrepl ixcheck ROOT --index ...   each index against the objects
objrepl check ROOT                 OK / WARN / FAIL (exit 0 / 1 / 2)
objrepl clear-alarm ROOT
objrepl status ROOT
objrepl engine                     the database engine (exit 0 for 64-bit, 1 for 32-bit)
objrepl takeover ROOT              a copy becomes primary: epoch + 1
objrepl rejoin ROOT                a former primary becomes a copy
Common: --name N --peer-name N --links SPEC --index SPEC --max-lag N --max-behind S
        --min-cert-days N --idle-timeout S --config FILE

A node is a folder (ROOT). Any option may come from ROOT/objrepl.conf (or --config FILE), one "key value" line each, the option without "--"; the command line wins. The keys are listed in the administrator's guide, section 2.3. objrepl primary is a test data generator: it writes test commits (adds, updates, removes, linked objects), sends them to the copy and waits up to 120 s for the copy to have them all, exit 0 (drained), 2 (not drained), 3 (refused), 4 (ROOT is a copy) or 64 (configuration or certificates). Programs write through the gxObjRepl API instead. objrepl copy runs until TERM or INT (Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Break on Windows), or until ROOT/objrepl.stop appears.

Examples

Two nodes on one machine, n1 (the primary) and n2 (the copy), in the current folder. Build the tool and check the engine; every node and program must use the same one (the default build is the 32-bit engine, -DDATAREEL_64BIT_DATABASE=ON makes the 64-bit one):

$ objrepl engine
engine 32-bit (file signature 8 bytes)

Certificates: utils/objrepl/objrepl_certs.sh makes a private CA, the copy's server certificate and the primary's client certificate (CN objrepl-primary). It is a dry run unless you add --apply, and it never overwrites a file:

$ utils/objrepl/objrepl_certs.sh certs --copy-host 127.0.0.1 --apply
CA       certs/ca.pem (CN objrepl-ca, 825 days)
copy     certs/copy.pem (CN objrepl-copy, subjectAltName IP:127.0.0.1)
primary  certs/primary.pem (CN objrepl-primary)
configs  certs/primary.conf certs/copy.conf
written to certs (keys mode 600)

The two configuration files:

$ cat n2/objrepl.conf
name n2
peer-name n1
ca certs/ca.pem
cert certs/copy.pem
key certs/copy.key
listen 127.0.0.1:24790
allow-cn objrepl-primary

$ cat n1/objrepl.conf
name n1
peer-name n2
ca certs/ca.pem
cert certs/primary.pem
key certs/primary.key
copy 127.0.0.1:24790

Start the copy, then send 200 test commits from the primary:

$ objrepl copy n2 > n2.log 2>&1 &  echo $! > n2.pid
$ cat n2.log
objrepl: copy listening on 127.0.0.1:24790 (gxStream, TLS, client CN objrepl-primary), applied 0, epoch 1

$ objrepl primary n1 --commits 200
objrepl primary: epoch 1, last seq 200, copy applied 200, 0 snapshot(s), outbox drained

Watch the nodes. check prints one line for cron or a monitor; here the primary is WARN only because no primary is running now (the generator has exited):

$ objrepl status n1
epoch 1 next_seq 201 acked_seq 200 applied_seq 0 in_snapshot 0 role primary digest dd6541189a6e5b70
$ objrepl status n2
epoch 1 next_seq 1 acked_seq 0 applied_seq 200 in_snapshot 0 role copy digest dd6541189a6e5b70

$ objrepl check n2
OK copy n2 epoch 1: applied 200 from n1, 202 frames, 176 tombstones, listening; last contact 0s ago
$ objrepl check n1
WARN primary n1 epoch 1: not running; seq 200, copy applied 200, lag 0 for 0s, oldest unacked 0s, outbox 0 (0 bytes), 176 tombstones, stopped, drained (not running, status 0s old)

Compare the two nodes: the same objects give the same digest output, whatever the file layouts:

$ objrepl digest n1 > n1.digest
objrepl digest: 176 tombstone(s) 280 stub(s) 0 dangling
$ objrepl digest n2 > n2.digest
objrepl digest: 176 tombstone(s) 277 stub(s) 0 dangling
$ cat n1.digest
objects 1025 digest 4dcf09fee9854aa8
$ cmp n1.digest n2.digest && echo "the same objects"
the same objects

A planned switch: stop the copy (by its process id), make it the primary at the next epoch, and make the old primary a copy. Its copy had every commit, so there is no full send:

$ kill $(cat n2.pid)
$ objrepl takeover n2
objrepl takeover: n2 is primary at epoch 2 (applied 200)
$ objrepl rejoin n1
objrepl rejoin: n1 is a copy at epoch 1, following on from seq 200 (its copy had every commit: no full send)

Swap the settings (n1 now listens on 127.0.0.1:24791 with the copy certificate and allows objrepl-primary; n2 sends to it with the primary certificate), start n1 as the copy and send 50 more commits from n2:

$ objrepl copy n1 > n1.log 2>&1 &  echo $! > n1.pid
$ objrepl primary n2 --commits 50
objrepl primary: epoch 2, last seq 250, copy applied 250, 0 snapshot(s), outbox drained
$ objrepl check n1
OK copy n1 epoch 2: applied 250 from n2, 52 frames, 232 tombstones, listening; last contact 0s ago
$ objrepl clear-alarm n1
no alarm
$ kill $(cat n1.pid)

The administrator's guide covers the same steps in more detail, failover after a crash, upgrades, troubleshooting and the plain file copy alternative.
